message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user is building "Vibe Voyager" — an interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering practices. It will be hosted at [REDACTED_DOMAIN] on Vercel free tier. The user has a lecture in ~1 week (from 2026-03-07). They want to use agent teams with Claude Code to build at scale (they've coded 50k+ lines in two days before). The user explicitly chose "subagent-driven development" in the current session to execute the implementation plan with parallel agent teams, with review checkpoints between phases.

   The user's preferences:
   - **Do NOT commit** CLAUDE.md, BUILD_LOG.md, docs/, .claude/ to git — these are gitignored
   - notebooklm-content was moved into docs/ folder
   - CLAUDE.md must include instructions to update BUILD_LOG.md before every session compaction
   - User wants BUILD_LOG updated after each phase completion

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Next.js 15.5.12** with App Router, TypeScript, React 19
   - **Tailwind CSS v4** — CSS-first config with `@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme` directive, NO tailwind.config.js
   - **Motion** package (v12.35.1) — import from `motion/react`, NOT `framer-motion`
   - **Howler.js** for audio (ambient loops + SFX sprites)
   - **HTML5 Canvas** for star map
   - **localStorage** for all game state (no backend, no database, no auth)
   - **Subagent-driven development** — fresh agent per task, parallel execution within phases
   - **9-phase implementation plan** with 39 tasks, up to 13 parallel agents at peak
   - **AnimatePresence** with `mode="wait"` for page transitions
   - **Glassmorphism** UI pattern: `bg-glass backdrop-blur-md border border-glass-border rounded-xl`

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/docs/plans/2026-03-07-implementation-plan.md`** — Master implementation plan with 9 phases, 39 tasks. Contains exact file paths, code scaffolding, dependency ordering, and parallelization strategy. This is the roadmap being executed.

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/docs/plans/2026-03-07-vibe-voyager-design.md`** — Design document. Updated in this session: fixed Academy section numbering (sections 8-9 renumbered, Section 10: Career Paths added).

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/CLAUDE.md`** — Project configuration. Updated with Build Log Protocol section and corrected file paths:
     ```
     ## Build Log Protocol
     - Before EVERY context compaction: update BUILD_LOG.md with current session progress
     - After completing each phase: log which agents ran, what was built, any decisions made
     - Track: agent count, files created, features completed, time spent, issues encountered
     ```
     Also updated: `3 Acts + Epilogue. 8 planets. 34 missions. 5 crew members. 4 player stats. 10 Academy sections.`

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/.gitignore`** — Updated to exclude:
     ```
     /docs/
     CLAUDE.md
     BUILD_LOG.md
     .claude/
     .playwright-mcp/
     ```

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/BUILD_LOG.md`** — Living build log. Updated with Phase 1 completion (4 commits, 2 agents), Phase 2 completion (1,835 lines, 4 parallel agents, 0 type errors), agent teams log, and running notes for 2026-03-08.

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/app/globals.css`** — Tailwind v4 theme with all design tokens (18 color tokens, 3 font families, 4 glow shadows, base styles, scrollbar, selection). Also has `@keyframes title-glow` animation added by title screen agent.

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/app/layout.tsx`** — Root layout with Google Fonts (Space Grotesk, Inter, JetBrains Mono), metadata, GameProvider wrapping children.

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/constants.ts`** — Shared constants: COLORS, RANKS, STATS, STAT_COLORS, STAT_LABELS, StatName type.

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/types.ts`** — All TypeScript interfaces: PlayerStats, GameState, Mission, MissionContent, DialogueNode, ChallengeData, CrewMember, InventoryItem, PlanetId, ShipType, Rank, etc. (103 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/game-state.ts`** — State management functions: createNewGame, saveGame, loadGame, deleteGame, hasSave, getRank, getTotalStats, isPlanetComplete, getPlanetStatus, completeMission, getCompletedMissionCount. Planet prerequisite chain defined. (144 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/game-context.tsx`** — React context: GameProvider, useGame hook. Loads from localStorage on mount, provides startNewGame, resetGame, completeMission, rank, totalStats, completedMissions. (74 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/components/ui/`** — 7 UI components:
     - `GlassPanel.tsx` — Glassmorphism container with glow variants, hover, polymorphic `as` prop
     - `StarfieldBackground.tsx` — Canvas-based 3-layer parallax starfield
     - `TypewriterText.tsx` — Character-by-character text reveal with cursor, click to skip
     - `StatGauge.tsx` — Animated horizontal stat bar with glow
     - `XPBar.tsx` — Rank progress bar with gradient
     - `Button.tsx` — 5 variants, 3 sizes, spring animations, focus-visible
     - `index.ts` — Barrel export

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/audio.ts`** — Singleton AudioManager wrapping Howler.js. SFX types: click, hover, warp, mission-complete, dialogue-blip, success, error, rank-up. (98 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/components/audio/AudioManager.tsx`** — AudioProvider context, useAudio hook, AudioToggle button component. Handles browser autoplay policy. (129 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/data/planets.ts`** — 8 planets with star map positions, prerequisites, colors, mission counts. TOTAL_MISSIONS=34, MISSION_COUNTS lookup.

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/data/missions.ts`** — All 34 mission stubs with metadata (id, planetId, title, challengeType, statRewards, order). Content arrays empty (to be filled in Phase 6). getMissionsByPlanet() and getMissionById() helpers. (513 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/data/crew.ts`** — 5 crew members: ARIA, Scout, Archie, Exec, Mirror with roles, agent phases, recruitment points, quotes. (74 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/data/items.ts`** — 7 inventory items with real-world tool mappings. (82 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/lib/data/academy.ts`** — 10 Academy section stubs. (90 lines)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/app/page.tsx`** — Title screen: StarfieldBackground, animated "VIBE VOYAGER" title with glow, staggered menu buttons (New Game, Continue, Academy, About), hasSave() check for Continue button. (133 lines changed)

   - **`/home/dev/vibe/app/create/page.tsx`** — 3-step character creation: callsign input, ship selection (Spark/Architect/Sentinel with SVGs), Star Wars text crawl, Launch button. AnimatePresence transitions between steps. Just completed by agent, needs commit.

   - **Memory files** updated:
     - `~/.claude/projects/-Users-shehral-vibe/memory/content-mapping.md` — Updated with expanded missions (34 total) and 10 Academy sections

4. Errors and Fixes:
   - **User rejected git add of project files**: User explicitly did not want CLAUDE.md, BUILD_LOG.md, docs/, notebooklm-content/, .claude/ committed to git. Fixed by adding all to .gitignore and moving notebooklm-content into docs/.
   - **User concern about committed files**: User asked "did you commit the claude.md and build log file when they weren't supposed to be committed?" — Verified via `git show --name-only` that they were NOT in any commit. Confirmed clean.
   - **Subagents couldn't run bash/git**: All 4 Phase 2 agents and Phase 3 agents completed their file creation but couldn't execute git commands. Fixed by having the main thread handle all commits after each agent completes.
   - **Design doc duplicate section numbering**: Academy sections 7 was duplicated (MCP Workshop and Resource Library both numbered 7). Fixed by renumbering to 7, 8, 9 and adding Section 10.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Adapted subagent-driven development skill for parallel execution — the skill says "never dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel" but the plan's tasks are designed with zero file overlap, so parallel dispatch is safe.
   - Handled context7's lack of Tailwind CSS v4 docs — used training knowledge for Tailwind v4 CSS-first configuration patterns.
   - Managed agent output by committing each agent's work from the main thread since agents lack bash permissions.

6. All User Messages:
   - "yes" (approve moving to implementation planning with writing-plans skill)
   - "what do you recommend?" (asking whether subagent-driven or parallel session execution)
   - "yes" (start Phase 1)
   - "did you commit the claude.md and build log file when they weren't supposed to be committed?"
   - "you're again adding files which i don't want added, put notebooklm content in the docs folder and gitignore the docs folder, do the same with claude.md and build_log but put instructions on claude.md to keep the build log file consistently updated before any session compacts etc"
   - "update build logs?" (after Phase 2 completed)
   - "yeah" (proceed to Phase 3)

7. Pending Tasks:
   - **Phase 3 agents still running**: Cockpit HUD (3.3), Star Map (3.4), Navigation Bar (3.5)
   - **Phase 3 agent completed but needs commit**: Character Creation (3.2) — `app/create/page.tsx` created, not yet committed
   - **Phases 4-9**: All pending after Phase 3 completes
   - Task tracking: Tasks #4 (Phase 3) is in_progress, #5-#9 are pending

8. Current Work:
   Phase 3 execution is in progress with 5 parallel agents. Two have completed:
   - Task 3.1 (Title Screen): Completed and committed
   - Task 3.2 (Character Creation): Completed, file created at `app/create/page.tsx`, NOT YET COMMITTED
   
   Three agents are still running:
   - Task 3.3 (Cockpit HUD): Building `app/cockpit/page.tsx`
   - Task 3.4 (Star Map): Building `app/starmap/page.tsx` and `components/game/StarMap.tsx`
   - Task 3.5 (Navigation Bar): Building `components/game/NavBar.tsx` and modifying `app/layout.tsx`

   The Task 3.2 notification just arrived. The agent created a 3-step character creation flow with callsign input, ship selection with SVG placeholders, and Star Wars-style text crawl. It needs to be committed:
   ```bash
   git add app/create/page.tsx
   git commit -m "feat: implement 3-step character creation flow"
   ```

9. Optional Next Step:
   Commit Task 3.2 (Character Creation) output immediately, then commit remaining Phase 3 agents as they complete (3.3, 3.4, 3.5). After all 5 Phase 3 agents are committed, run type-check, update BUILD_LOG, mark Phase 3 complete, and proceed to Phase 4 (3 parallel agents: Dialogue System, Mission Framework, Inventory/Crew Pages).

   The user's flow is: Phase 1 ✅ → Phase 2 ✅ → Phase 3 (in progress, 2/5 done) → Phase 4 → Phase 5 → Phase 6+7 → Phase 8 → Phase 9.

   Git log so far (8 commits):
   ```
   02f1168 feat: create title screen with animated starfield and menu
   f054f23 feat: define game data layer — planets, missions, crew, items, academy
   0f4c2aa feat: implement Howler.js audio system with SFX and ambient support
   2d1436c feat: create glassmorphism UI component library
   89232ff feat: implement game state management with localStorage persistence
   e8127e6 chore: gitignore playwright-mcp artifacts
   0435457 feat: configure Tailwind v4 design system with color tokens and typography
   3d44215 chore: gitignore docs, CLAUDE.md, BUILD_LOG.md, and .claude
   f847895 chore: scaffold Next.js 15 project with TypeScript and Tailwind v4
   ```

If you need specific details from before compaction (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /home/dev/[REDACTED_PROJECT]

    58→    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    59→      const layer = Math.random()
    60→      let speed: number, size: number, opacity: number

    62→        // Distant layer
    63→        speed = 0.08
    64→        size = Math.random() * 1 + 0.5
    65→        opacity = Math.random() * 0.3 + 0.1
    66→      } else if (layer < 0.85) {

    69→        size = Math.random() * 1.5 + 1
    70→        opacity = Math.random() * 0.4 + 0.3
    71→      } else {

    88→  // Count completed missions for a planet
    89→  const getCompletedCount = useCallback(

   295→      // Academy station at top (diamond shape)

   297→        ACADEMY_POSITION.x,

   302→      const academyPulse = 0.7 + Math.sin(t * 1.5) * 0.3

   311→      ctx.fillStyle = '#4a6fa5'

   407→      const clickY = e.clientY - rect.top

   409→      const height = window.innerHeight
   410→
   411→      // Check academy click

   460→      const height = window.innerHeight

   464→      // Check academy

   496→      onMouseMove={handleMouseMove}

   498→    />
   499→  )

# How This Was Built: A Claude Code Case Study

> This document tracks the entire process of building [REDACTED_DOMAIN] using Claude Code with agent teams, plugins, and skills. It serves as both a behind-the-scenes look and living proof of the agentic development practices taught on the platform.

## Build Metadata
- **Start Date:** 2026-03-07
- **Target:** Full game experience in ~1 week
- **Stack:** Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Canvas, Howler.js
- **Hosting:** Vercel (free tier)
- **Primary Tool:** Claude Code (Opus 4.6)

## Phase 1: Brainstorming & Design
- **Approach:** Used `superpowers:brainstorming` skill for structured design exploration
- **Decisions made through dialogue:**
  - Audience: Mixed levels (beginner to advanced)
  - Format: Full game experience (not just a course with game skin)
  - Narrative: Space exploration — Solo Pilot → First Contact → Fleet Commander → Academy
  - Visual style: Clean minimalist sci-fi (glassmorphism, Framer Motion, SVG)
  - Audio: Full soundscape (ambient + UI SFX)
  - Tech: Next.js + HTML5 Canvas (no game engine — agents parallelize React better)
  - Academy: Hybrid format (space aesthetic, real-world content)
- **Content base:** NotebookLM deep research — 15-slide PDF, mind map, infographic, 57+ curated sources, beginner's guide doc, key findings spreadsheet

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Motion v12 strict types:** Unlike framer-motion, the `motion` package enforces strict literal types in `Variants`. When you define `transition: { type: 'spring' }` as a plain object, TypeScript infers `type` as `string` — but Motion expects a specific union type like `'spring' | 'tween' | 'inertia'`. The fix is `as const` on the object or `type: 'spring' as const` on the property. This is a common gotcha when migrating from framer-motion to motion.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

# Vibe Voyager — Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Build a complete interactive space exploration game that teaches vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern software engineering — from beginner to agentic developer.

**Architecture:** Next.js 15 App Router with client-side game state in localStorage. No backend. All game content defined as TypeScript data structures. Canvas-based star map. Motion for animations. Howler.js for audio. Glassmorphism UI throughout.

**Tech Stack:** Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Motion (from `motion/react`), HTML5 Canvas, Howler.js, localStorage, Vercel

**Parallelization:** Tasks within each phase are independent and SHOULD be dispatched to parallel agents. Dependencies between phases are noted. Each task produces a working, committable unit.

**Critical Rules:**
- Import Motion from `motion/react`, NEVER from `framer-motion`
- Tailwind v4: use `@import "tailwindcss"` + `@theme` in CSS, NOT `tailwind.config.js`
- ALWAYS check context7 before writing components to verify latest API patterns
- All game state in localStorage — no backend, no database, no auth
- Update `BUILD_LOG.md` after completing each phase

**Implementation:**
- Scenario description at top (e.g., "Write a prompt to build a todo app with user auth")
- Textarea for player to write prompt
- "Submit" button
- Scoring: check for required keywords/concepts (case-insensitive). Each concept = 1 point.
- Show results: which concepts were covered, which were missed
- Visual: green checkmarks for hits, red X for misses
- Score = concepts_found / total_concepts * 100
- Props: `{ scenario: string, requiredConcepts: string[], onComplete: (score: number) => void }`

**Commit:** `feat: implement Prompt Duel mini-game with keyword scoring`

### Task 5.2: Architect Mini-Game

**Files:**
- Create: `components/games/Architect.tsx`

**Mechanic:** Drag-and-drop nodes to build system diagrams. Player arranges components in correct order/structure.

**Implementation:**
- Left sidebar: draggable node tiles (labeled boxes)
- Center: drop zone canvas/grid
- Pre-defined connection points or slots where nodes should go
- Player drags nodes from sidebar into correct slots
- Visual feedback: slot highlights green when correct node is near, red when wrong
- Score based on correctly placed nodes / total nodes
- For simpler variant: ordered list — drag items into correct sequence
- Uses HTML drag-and-drop API (onDrag, onDragOver, onDrop) — no external library
- Props: `{ nodes: ArchNode[], slots: ArchSlot[], onComplete: (score: number) => void }`
- Mobile: tap to select, tap slot to place

**Commit:** `feat: implement Architect drag-and-drop diagram builder`

### Task 5.3: Connect Mini-Game

**Files:**
- Create: `components/games/Connect.tsx`

**Mechanic:** Draw connections between items on left and right columns (matching puzzle). Used for MCP wiring, agent-tool connections.

**Implementation:**
- Left column: source items (labeled boxes)
- Right column: target items (labeled boxes)
- Player clicks source, then clicks target to create a connection line
- Connection line drawn as SVG path between the two
- Click existing connection to remove it
- Correct connections glow green on submit, wrong ones glow red
- Score = correct_connections / total_connections * 100
- Props: `{ sources: string[], targets: string[], correctPairs: [number, number][], onComplete: (score: number) => void }`

**Commit:** `feat: implement Connect wiring puzzle mini-game`

### Task 5.4: Debug Mini-Game

**Files:**
- Create: `components/games/Debug.tsx`

**Mechanic:** Find problems in code or architecture. Player clicks on buggy lines or selects issues from a list.

**Implementation:**
- Code block displayed in JetBrains Mono with line numbers
- Player clicks lines they think contain bugs
- Selected lines highlight with terracotta border
- "Submit" button checks selections against known bug lines
- Results: correct selections in green, missed bugs in red with explanation
- Alternative mode: multiple-choice list of issues (select all that apply)
- Score = (correct_selections - false_positives) / total_bugs * 100 (min 0)

**Implementation:**

     3→import { createContext, useContext, useState, useCallback, useEffect, ReactNode } from 'react'
     4→import { GameState, PlayerStats, ShipType } from './types'
     5→import { createNewGame, saveGame, loadGame, deleteGame, completeMission as completeMissionFn, getRank, getTotalStats, getCompletedMissionCount } from './game-state'
     6→
     7→interface GameContextType {
     8→  state: GameState | null
     9→  loading: boolean
    10→  startNewGame: (callsign: string, ship: ShipType) => void
    11→  resetGame: () => void
    12→  completeMission: (missionId: string, score: number, statRewards: Partial<PlayerStats>, itemReward?: string, crewReward?: string) => void
    13→  rank: string
    14→  totalStats: number
    15→  completedMissions: number
    16→}
    17→
    18→const GameContext = createContext<GameContextType | null>(null)
    19→
    20→export function GameProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
    21→  const [state, setState] = useState<GameState | null>(null)
    22→  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true)
    23→
    24→  useEffect(() => {
    25→    const saved = loadGame()
    26→    setState(saved)
    27→    setLoading(false)
    28→  }, [])
    29→
    30→  const startNewGame = useCallback((callsign: string, ship: ShipType) => {
    31→    const newState = createNewGame(callsign, ship)
    32→    saveGame(newState)
    33→    setState(newState)
    34→  }, [])
    35→
    36→  const resetGame = useCallback(() => {
    37→    deleteGame()
    38→    setState(null)
    39→  }, [])
    40→
    41→  const completeMissionCb = useCallback((missionId: string, score: number, statRewards: Partial<PlayerStats>, itemReward?: string, crewReward?: string) => {
    42→    setState(prev => {
    43→      if (!prev) return prev
    44→      return completeMissionFn(prev, missionId, score, statRewards, itemReward, crewReward)
    45→    })
    46→  }, [])
    47→
    48→  const rank = state ? getRank(state.stats) : 'Cadet'
    49→  const totalStats = state ? getTotalStats(state.stats) : 4
    50→  const completedMissions = state ? getCompletedMissionCount(state) : 0
    51→
    52→  return (
    53→    <GameContext.Provider value={{
    54→      state,
    55→      loading,
    56→      startNewGame,
    57→      resetGame,
    58→      completeMission: completeMissionCb,
    59→      rank,
    60→      totalStats,
    61→      completedMissions,
    62→    }}>
    63→      {children}
    64→    </GameContext.Provider>
    65→  )
    66→}
    67→
    68→export function useGame() {
    69→  const context = useContext(GameContext)
    70→  if (!context) {
    71→    throw new Error('useGame must be used within a GameProvider')
    72→  }
    73→  return context
    74→}

5. `app/planets/[planetId]/mission/[missionId]/page.tsx` (mission page)

## Design System Context
- Import Motion from `motion/react` (NOT framer-motion). Use AnimatePresence for transitions.
- Use `clsx` for class composition (already installed)
- Glass panel style: `bg-glass backdrop-blur-md border border-glass-border rounded-xl`
- Colors: void (#0a0f1a), nebula (#4a6fa5), signal (#6b9e78), terracotta (#c17147), starlight (#e8e0d4), starlight-dim (muted)
- Font classes: `font-display` (Space Grotesk), `font-body` (Inter), `font-mono` (JetBrains Mono)
- Use existing components from `@/components/ui`: GlassPanel, StarfieldBackground, TypewriterText, Button, StatGauge
- Use `as const` on any transition type literals to avoid Motion type errors (e.g., `type: 'spring' as const`)

## Key Types (from lib/types.ts)
```typescript
export type ChallengeType = 'prompt-duel' | 'architect' | 'connect' | 'debug' | 'command' | 'dialogue'
export type PlanetId = 'vibe-world' | 'debt-belt' | 'mcp-station' | 'agent-academy' | 'framework-nebula' | 'orchestration-citadel' | 'security-fortress' | 'production-worlds'
export type MissionStatus = 'locked' | 'available' | 'in_progress' | 'completed'

export interface Mission {
  id: string; planetId: PlanetId; title: string; subtitle: string; description: string
  challengeType: ChallengeType; statRewards: Partial<PlayerStats>
  itemReward?: string; crewReward?: string; order: number; content: MissionContent
}

export interface MissionContent {
  briefing: DialogueNode[]; learning: LearningBlock[]; challenge: ChallengeData; debrief: DialogueNode[]
}

export interface LearningBlock {
  type: 'text' | 'code' | 'stat' | 'image'; content: string; highlight?: boolean
}

export interface ChallengeData {
  type: ChallengeType; instructions: string; data: Record<string, unknown>; passingScore: number
}

export interface DialogueNode { speaker: string; text: string; choices?: DialogueChoice[] }
export interface DialogueChoice { text: string; correct?: boolean; response?: string }
```

```typescript
// from @/lib/data/planets

// Planet has: id, name, subtitle, act, description, color, position, prerequisites, missionCount

// from @/lib/game-state  
import { getPlanetStatus, getMissionProgress } from '@/lib/game-state'

// from @/lib/game-context
import { useGame } from '@/lib/game-context'
// useGame() returns: { state, loading, completeMission, rank, totalStats, completedMissions }
// completeMission(missionId, score, statRewards, itemReward?, crewReward?)
```

## File 1: MissionBriefing.tsx
Props: `{ mission: Mission; onBegin: () => void }`
- Full GlassPanel with mission title and subtitle
- ARIA dialogue text (use TypewriterText for briefing[0].text if available, else mission.description)
- Challenge type icon/label
- "Begin Mission" Button at bottom

## File 2: LearningPhase.tsx
Props: `{ blocks: LearningBlock[]; onProceed: () => void }`
- Scrollable content area inside GlassPanel
- Renders blocks by type:
  - `text`: paragraph with `font-body text-starlight`
  - `code`: preformatted code block with `font-mono text-sm bg-void/50 p-4 rounded-lg border border-glass-border` and overflow-x-auto
  - `stat`: highlighted stat callout with terracotta left border and bg-terracotta/10
  - `image`: placeholder div (images will come later)
- `highlight` flag makes text blocks glow with a left border
- "Proceed to Challenge" Button at bottom

## File 3: MissionDebrief.tsx
Props: `{ mission: Mission; score: number; onNext: () => void; onReturn: () => void }`
- Score display: 0-100 percentage, with star rating (score >= 90: 3 stars, >= 60: 2 stars, else 1 star)
- Stars rendered as SVG or unicode ★/☆
- Stat gains section: show each stat reward with +N label, animated
- Item/crew reward card if mission has itemReward or crewReward
- Two buttons: "Next Mission" and "Return to Planet"

## File 4: Planet Landing Page — app/planets/[planetId]/page.tsx
- 'use client'
- Get planetId from params (Next.js 15 App Router: `params` is a Promise, use `React.use(params)`)
- StarfieldBackground
- Planet header: name, subtitle, act label, description
- List of missions as GlassPanel cards:
  - Each shows: mission order number, title, subtitle, challenge type label, status indicator
  - Status: locked (dim, no click), available (pulsing border), in_progress (terracotta glow), completed (signal checkmark)
  - Determine status: first mission is always available if planet is available. Later missions available if previous mission is completed.
  - Click available/in-progress → navigate to `/planets/[planetId]/mission/[missionId]`
- "Return to Star Map" Button at top or bottom → `/starmap`
- Use `useGame()` to get state for status checks, `getMissionsByPlanet(planetId)` for mission list

## File 5: Mission Page — app/planets/[planetId]/mission/[missionId]/page.tsx
- 'use client'
- Get params (planetId, missionId) from Next.js 15 params Promise
- 4-phase flow managed by state variable `phase`: 'briefing' | 'learning' | 'challenge' | 'debrief'
- Phase 1: MissionBriefing → onBegin sets phase to 'learning'
- Phase 2: LearningPhase → onProceed sets phase to 'challenge'
- Phase 3: Challenge → For now, render a placeholder GlassPanel that says "Challenge: [challengeType]" with a "Complete (Mock)" button that calls handleChallengeComplete with score 80
- Phase 4: MissionDebrief → onNext navigates to next mission, onReturn navigates to planet page
- On challenge complete: call `completeMission(missionId, score, mission.statRewards, mission.itemReward, mission.crewReward)` from useGame()
- AnimatePresence between phases
- Redirect to home if no game state loaded

All files should be 'use client'. Do NOT import `cn` — use `clsx` directly.

- GlassPanel container
- Instructions text at top: "Find the bugs in this code. Click on the lines you think contain issues."
- Code display:
  - Split code by newlines, render each line as a clickable row
  - Line numbers on the left in text-starlight-dim font-mono text-xs
  - Code text in font-mono text-sm text-starlight
  - Background: bg-void/50 with border-glass-border

- "Submit" Button (enabled when at least 1 line selected)
- Scoring:
  - correct_selections = lines selected that are in bugLines
  - false_positives = lines selected that are NOT in bugLines
  - Score = Math.max(0, ((correct_selections - false_positives) / bugLines.length) * 100)
- Results view:
  - Each line shows its result:
    - Correctly found bugs: signal (green) left border + checkmark + explanation
    - False positives: terracotta (red) left border + X + "No bug here"
    - Missed bugs: yellow/amber left border + "!" + explanation + "Missed!"
  - Score percentage at top
  - "Continue" Button calls onComplete(score)

<result>The component is complete. Here is a summary of what was created:

**File created:** `/home/dev/vibe/components/games/Connect.tsx`

**Component overview:**

- **`'use client'`** directive for client-side interactivity
- Imports `motion` and `AnimatePresence` from `motion/react` (correct package), `clsx` for class composition, and `GlassPanel`/`Button` from the existing UI library
- Uses `as const` on all transition type string literals

**Architecture:**

- **State management:** Tracks `connections` (active pairs), `selectedSource` (click-to-connect flow), `results` (post-check feedback), and `score`
- **Position tracking:** Uses `useRef` maps for source/target DOM elements and `getBoundingClientRect()` to calculate SVG line endpoints relative to the container. Recalculates on resize and when props change.
- **SVG overlay:** Absolutely positioned SVG covering the container, with `pointer-events-none` on the SVG itself but `pointer-events: stroke` on individual connection paths so they can be clicked to remove

**Interaction flow:**

1. Click a source item -- it highlights with a nebula ring glow
2. Click a target item -- creates a curved bezier SVG connection line (animated with Motion `pathLength`)
3. Re-clicking a connected source replaces the old connection
4. Click an existing connection line to remove it
5. "Check Connections" button appears once at least one connection exists
6. On check: correct connections glow signal green, wrong ones glow terracotta red, missed connections appear as dashed green lines
7. Score displayed as percentage, then "Continue" button calls `onComplete(score)`

**Key design decisions:**

- Click handlers are on wrapper `div` elements rather than on `GlassPanel` directly, since `GlassPanel` doesn't accept `onClick` in its props interface
- `GlassPanel`'s own `hover` prop handles the scale/color hover animation, avoiding double-animation conflicts
- Connection lines use cubic bezier curves with control point offsets of 40% of the horizontal distance (minimum 60px) for a pleasing curved look
- Responsive: uses `grid-cols-1` on mobile and `grid-cols-[1fr_auto_1fr]` on desktop, with SVG lines still connecting items in both layouts</result>
